title: Lord, Must We Die? O Let Us Die
description: Lord, Must We Die? O Let Us Die in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 539 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Happy Death”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, must we die? O let us die Trust-ing in thee a-lone! Our liv-ing tes-ti-mo-ny given, Then leave our dy-ing one.

lines: Lord, must we die? O let us die
If we must die, O let us die
And change these fleeting joys below
If we must die, — as die we must, —
And bear us on his friendly wing
Of Canaan's land, from Pisgah's top,
May we but have a view!
Though Jordan should o'erflow its banks,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
